items.titleEn: A group of 9 united voters raised $128 for 26 bus routes to return to their hometowns
items.summaryEn: After the elections, the number of people who have returned to their homeland began to rise on the afternoon of today (March 27). Due to the demand for freight, the railway has opened 71 more trains from 5pm to 8pm, and has also introduced free-seat access controls at South Port, Taipei and Brunei stations. The train is scheduled to open 88 more routes, while the national highway passenger service will provide 24-hour shuttle service. In addition, to reduce the burden of youth returning home, private groups have also launched a private car to return home through fundraising. However, the evacuation from the island was affected by the weather, and Kimmen Owl was affected by bad weather, the voting boats were cancelled, and hundreds of voters were unable to return home to vote.

items.titleEn: Meta lenses threatened privacy: Dutch publicists demand a ban on sale
items.summaryEn: Thanksgiving is over, and soon it will be Christmas, and many people are looking forward to Christmas gifts that include all sorts of AI products. Meta has a pair of artificial intelligence glasses developed in partnership with parent company Rappon, which have been a global hit and recently hit plates in the Netherlands. A private group has filed a lawsuit alleging that the lens could have been used to film unknown footage in high-risk areas, including changing rooms, swimming pools and beaches. They believe that this is a violation of European privacy laws, and demand that a judge order a ban on the sale. However, Meta's lawyers argue that a video indicator light on the lens has been designed with a reminder function and that manufacturers should not be held responsible for all intentional abuse. Since its launch, the popular AI lens has sold more than 10 million copies, accounting for 80% of the market share. A Dutch chain of stores has temporarily suspended the product after the lawsuit was filed, and privacy regulators have urged people not to buy ...

items.summaryEn: According to statistics, the number of Japanese school bullies and students refusing to attend school is on the rise.
